title: Choose Cells' layout
question: Same Swiss Grid world in cobalt, three ways to lay out a spreadsheet. The roll dealt the sheet strip. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Sheet strip
options.lineage: The Jotbook page strip, applied to sheets
options.thesis: The workbook's sheets are numbered down a strip beside the grid, each with a row-count bar, the way Jotbook numbers its pages.
options.viewport: Cobalt rail, a bar reading Cells / Channel numbers 2026, a formula line, a 240px strip of numbered sheets, and the grid across the rest.
options.risk: The strip takes 240px from the grid, so fewer columns fit on screen.

options.label: Readout bar
options.lineage: The suite's numerals, applied to the active cell
options.thesis: The grid runs full width under a readout that shows the active cell's address as a 42px numeral, its formula and its value; sheets are numbered tabs along the bottom.
options.viewport: Cobalt rail, the command bar, a 72px readout (C7, =SUM(C2:C6), 523,587), the full-width grid, and sheet tabs with Sum, Average and Count.
options.risk: The closest to a familiar spreadsheet; the readout is its one new idea.

options.label: Figures column
options.lineage: A live summary of whatever you select
options.thesis: Select any range and a column beside the grid shows its sum as a large numeral, the other figures, and a ready chart you can insert.
options.viewport: Cobalt rail, the command bar, a formula line, the grid with C2:C6 selected, a 296px figures column, and numbered sheet tabs.
options.risk: The column is always open and takes width even when nothing worth summing is selected.
